title: What If Your Air Mattress Became a Business?
description:
How did one air mattress turn into 2.5 billion guest stays?

Sources:
- Wikipedia: Airbnb: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbnb
- Airbnb Help Center: Airbnb service fees: https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1857
- Airbnb Newsroom: About us: https://news.airbnb.com/about-us/

Wikipedia (Airbnb): October 2007, roommates Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia put an air mattress in their San Francisco living room to help pay rent; the founders raised $30,000 selling cereal named after the 2008 presidential candidates; Airbnb acts as a broker and charges a commission on each booking. Airbnb Help Center: under the single-fee structure most hosts pay 15.5%; under the older split fee, most hosts pay 3% and guests 14.1% to 16.5%. Airbnb newsroom: over 5.5 million hosts and over 2.5 billion guest arrivals. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: How did one air mattress turn into 2.5 billion guest stays?
Just two roommates, short on rent. So they rented out an air mattress.
Then, to keep going, they sold cereal. 30,000 dollars.
But here's the money flip. Airbnb keeps a cut of every booking. Most hosts pay 15.5 percent.
Today? Over 5.5 million hosts. Over 2.5 billion arrivals.
